# UX Requirements Quality Checklist: Progress Step Navigation

**Purpose**: Evaluate completeness, clarity, consistency, and measurability of the progress-step UX requirements
**Created**: 2026-09-17
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact generated by `/speckit-checklist`.
**Review Ownership**: Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines that the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied. Checkbox state does not indicate implementation completion.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are current, completed, pending, and invalid step states each defined with distinct required outcomes? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002, §FR-003, §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK002 Are requirements defined for both direct step selection and existing sequential form progression? [Completeness, Spec §User Story 2, §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK003 Are data-preservation requirements stated for every navigation direction and destination state? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK004 Does the specification define the accessible naming and keyboard requirements for every interactive step control? [Completeness, Spec §FR-007, §FR-008]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK005 Is the phrase "passed its required validation" tied to an explicit validation authority and defined field scope? [Clarity, Ambiguity, Spec §FR-003, Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK006 Is the distinction between an unvisited pending step and an invalid step clear enough to determine their visual and semantic treatment? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002, §FR-004, data-model.md]
- [ ] CHK007 Is the rule for selecting a future step before the current step is complete explicit about whether navigation is allowed and what feedback is provided? [Clarity, Spec §User Story 2, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK008 Are "accessible name," "keyboard activation," and "without relying on color alone" defined with objective content expectations? [Clarity, Spec §FR-007, §FR-008, §FR-009]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK009 Do the requirements consistently allow review of incomplete sections while also preventing incomplete steps from appearing completed? [Consistency, Spec §FR-003, §FR-005, Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK010 Are the check-icon rule, completion-state model, and success criterion aligned on whether the active step can ever display a completion check? [Consistency, Spec §FR-003, data-model.md, SC-001]
- [ ] CHK011 Do the preservation requirements remain consistent with the stated scope exclusion for form validation, submission, and persistence behavior? [Consistency, Spec §FR-006, Assumptions]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK012 Can the 100% check-icon outcome be evaluated from an unambiguous definition of a validated completed step? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001, §FR-003]
- [ ] CHK013 Is the one-selection navigation target measurable for every configured step, including the current step and future steps? [Measurability, Spec §SC-002, §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK014 Are the exact cardinality rules for indicators and connectors specified for every configured step-list length? [Measurability, Spec §SC-004, §FR-001, §FR-011]
- [ ] CHK015 Can the requirement to distinguish states without color alone be evaluated using specified non-color cues? [Measurability, Spec §SC-005, §FR-009]

## Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK016 Are primary scenarios complete for first entry, successful progression, direct review, correction, and return to a completed section? [Coverage, Spec §User Story 1, §User Story 2]
- [ ] CHK017 Are alternate navigation scenarios complete for selecting the current step and selecting a future step with incomplete data? [Coverage, Spec Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK018 Are exception and recovery requirements complete for a previously completed step becoming invalid after edits? [Coverage, Recovery Flow, Spec Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK019 Is the configured step-list change scenario intentionally bounded and sufficiently specified, rather than relying on an implicit fixed count of three? [Coverage, Spec Edge Cases, §FR-001]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK020 Are accessibility requirements defined for focus visibility, control semantics, keyboard operation, and state announcement, not only control reachability? [Accessibility, Completeness, Spec §FR-007, §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK021 Is the requirement for immediate progress-state updates quantified with an observable responsiveness threshold? [Performance, Clarity, Plan §Technical Context]
- [ ] CHK022 Are visual distinctions for all four completion states specified consistently across icon, text, and other non-color cues? [Accessibility, Consistency, Spec §FR-009, data-model.md]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK023 Is the dependency on the existing validation behavior documented with enough detail to prevent competing completion rules? [Dependency, Assumption, Spec Assumptions, Plan §Technical Context]
- [ ] CHK024 Are the existing three form sections identified as the initial scope while keeping the generic configured-step behavior unambiguous? [Scope, Assumption, Spec Assumptions, §FR-001]
- [ ] CHK025 Are unchanged form submission, persistence, and API behaviors explicitly separated from the progress-state requirements? [Dependency, Scope, Spec Assumptions, Plan §Technical Context]

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [ ] CHK026 Is the phrase "available step indicator" defined so users and implementers share the same navigation eligibility rules? [Ambiguity, Spec §User Story 2, §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK027 Does the specification resolve whether an invalid previously completed step should remain visually distinct from a never-visited pending step? [Ambiguity, Spec Edge Cases, data-model.md]
- [ ] CHK028 Are the meanings of "current," "completed," "pending," and "invalid" consistent across the spec, data model, UI contract, and plan? [Traceability, Consistency, Spec §FR-002, data-model.md, contracts/progress-steps-ui.md]

## Notes

- All items are intentionally unchecked for reviewer evaluation.
- This checklist validates the quality of the English requirements, not the application implementation.
- `/speckit-implement` may read checklist state as a gate but must not modify these markers.
- Add reviewer findings or links inline without changing the meaning of the checklist items.
